manifest.name: dsh-zcode-memory
manifest.description: ZCode-compatible project memory, ZCode memory import, and a memory settings page for DeepSeek Harness

bundle.text:
# dsh-zcode bundle patch: inserts the plugin row into every profile that adds
# this package as a bundle (`dsh plugin --profile <name> add ./dsh-zcode`).
# The same row carries the host plugin (package main) and the web client module
# (package.json dsh.client); the user's cordis.patch.yml can override `config`.
- insert:
    - id: zcode-memory
      name: dsh-zcode-memory
      config:
        enabled: true

readme.text:
ZCode-compatible project memory, a post-turn changed-files panel with review/open actions, and a memory settings page for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

**Compatibility: dsh `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0`** (declared via `engines.dsh`; verified against `0.2.1-rc.3`, `0.2.1-rc.5`, and `0.2.2-rc.1` — the latter on cordis 4.1.0 / schemastery 3.19.0). The installer refuses to run against an incompatible dsh. For dsh 0.1.x use plugin [v0.1.0](https://github.com/gniquil123/dsh-zcode-memory/releases/tag/v0.1.0).

1. **ZCode-compatible project memory** — per-project memory directories whose names follow the exact same encoding rule as ZCode (`basename slug` + `-` + first 16 hex of SHA-256 over the normalized absolute path, lowercased on Windows). Copy ZCode's `memories/projects/` tree into this plugin's memory root and every project resolves to the same directories, ready to reuse and maintain. Each agent session receives one context injection teaching the model the memory protocol (four memory types, frontmatter format, `MEMORY.md` index rules) plus the project's current index; writes inside the memory root are sandbox-auto-allowed, mirroring ZCode's memory file permission.
2. **Post-turn changed files** — on dsh 0.1.x, plugin v0.1.0 rendered a turn-tail panel with a **Review** button (inline +/- diff) and an **Open** button. On dsh 0.2.x the official `dsh-workspace-changes` + deliverables UI provides this natively (turn tail with per-file diff and open actions), so this plugin no longer ships its own panel and defers to it.
3. **Settings page** — a dedicated "ZCode Memory" section in the web settings:
   - view/edit the memory root (persisted to `<dsh-home>/dsh-zcode-memory.json`); a **Bro
> Fully compatible with ZCode project memory directories: copy ZCode's `memories/projects` tree into the memory root and it is reused as-is.
Prerequisites: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) ≥ 20 with npm (`dsh` and `pnpm` are located automatically — no PATH setup needed).

```sh
tar -xzf dsh-zcode-memory-0.1.0.tgz && node dsh-zcode-memory/install.mjs
```

`install.mjs` registers the plugin into the `web` profile via the official `dsh plugin add` flow and links every peer dependency to the running dsh installation, so the plugin and the host share one module instance. Options: `--profile <name>` (default `web`), `--home <dsh-home>` (default `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`), `--dsh <dir>` (override auto-detection).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/gniquil123/dsh-zcode-memory.git
node dsh-zcode-memory/install.mjs
```

The `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron app — the CLI refuses `dsh plugin add` there. Install manually (same pattern as any third-party desktop bundle):

1. Edit `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`: add `"dsh-zcode-memory": "link:<path-to-clone>"` to `dependencies` and `"dsh-zcode-memory"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`.
2. Run `pnpm install` in that directory.
3. Restart the DeepSeek Harness desktop app.
Then restart the profile: `dsh web`. The settings page gains a "ZCode Memory" section.
```sh

Copy-Item -Recurse "$env:USERPROFILE\.zcode\cli\memories\projects" "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\memories\projects"
```

```sh

cp -r ~/.zcode/cli/memories/projects ~/.dsh/memories/projects
```

Memory root defaults to `<dsh-home>/memories`; projects live at `<root>/projects/<project-key>/memory/`. Keys are computed exactly like ZCode's, so the copy is recognized as-is.

Edit the profile's user patch layer (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: zcode-memory
  config:
    enabled: true            # false disables injection and the remote service
    memoryRoot: ""           # non-empty overrides the root (wins over the settings page value)

Runtime changes made on the settings page persist to `<dsh-home>/dsh-zcode-memory.json`; a patch-configured `memoryRoot` always wins.

- `memoryWriteAllow` widens the sandbox policy **only** for `writeText`/`editText` calls whose resolved target lies inside the memory root — the equivalent of ZCode's auto-allowed memory writes. Bash and all other paths keep the session's standing mode. Set it to `false` if you prefer approving memory writes manually.
- Injected memory content is model-readable context, exactly like ZCode: memory files are written by the model, and consumers must verify freshness before recommending from them (the injected protocol includes that instruction).

- `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` written by a newer dsh desktop build uses a rich format that `0.1.0-rc.6`'s flat parser rejects. If you run both, point the web profile's `credentials` row at a separate file via the user patch layer:

```yaml
  - id: credentials
    config:
      path: '<dsh-home>/.credentials-web.yaml'
      dshHome: '<dsh-home>'

- Host half (`lib/index.js`): injects the memory context once per session on `agent/pre-step` (mid-session re-injection would wake the agent loop into a spurious reply); wraps `ctx.fs.writeText/editText` for the memory-root allowance; registers a Typert Remote gateway.
- Remote channel: `lib/typert.host.js` is a hand-written generator-format Typert contract (`dsh-typert-loader` auto-registers any mounted package's `./typert` export); the client half mounts its descriptors through the public `ctx.remote.$mount`. Self-mounted namespaces must NOT be declared in the module's `inject` (that deadlocks the boot waiting on a service only the module itself creates) — calls resolve through `remote.namespaces`.
- Changed-files: pure client-side derivation over the conversation event stream, following the official deliverables plugin's accumulator pattern. The turn tail is a chain slot electing the first non-null selector in ascending `priority`; this panel registers at `priority: -1` so it wins when diffs were captured and defers to the official produced-files panel otherwise.
- `lib/project-key.js` is ported 1:1 from ZCode (`zai-org/ZCode`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/core/src/memory/project-ro

- **Fixed a startup crash when the plugin is link-mounted by the dsh desktop app** — `zod` used to live only in `dependencies`, but dsh desktop's module router redirects a linked plugin's bare imports to the app's built-in shared copies ONLY for names listed in **peerDependencies** (and present in the runtime resolution table); `dependencies` entries fall back to native resolution, which walks up from the plugin's real path and finds nothing — `import { z } from "zod"` in `lib/typert.host.js` threw `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, the typert-loader failed loud, the `settings/describe` RPC answered not-ok, and the Electron main process crashed with `desktop welcome: Web RPC failed`. `zod` (`^4.0.0`) is now also declared in `peerDependencies`, so the router resolves the app's own zod (0.2.2-rc.1 ships zod@4.4.3 — no copy drift); `dependencies.zod` is kept, leaving regular GitHub/profile installs unaffected. The smoke test gained a regression guard asserting `zod` must be present in peerDependencies.

- **Verified against dsh 0.2.2-rc.1** — after the desktop app upgraded to 0.2.2-rc.1 (cordis 4.1.0 / schemastery 3.19.0), the plugin keeps working unchanged; `engines.dsh` and the peer ranges are unchanged (already covered).
- **Fixed the settings page ZCode tab rendering blank** — the v0.2.5 one-click switch missed declaring the `adopting`/`adoptResult` states, so rendering threw a ReferenceError that blanked the whole settings section; declarations added, and every identifier introduced this cycle was audited for declaration/reference pairing.
- **Mode-aware UI** — `status` gains `sameStore` (the effective root compared against the ZCode store's realpath, with Windows case/separator normalization): the status area shows a mode badge (shared store / local); when already on the shared store, the import card collapses into a note and the "Use ZCode shared store" button becomes a disabled "On shared store" — import no longer conflicts with the same-store semantics in shared-store mode.
- **Root card relayout** — the path input and **Browse…** share one row (the input fills the remaining width so long UNC paths stay fully visible); **Open folder / Save / Use shared store / Refresh** m

- **One-click switch of the memory root to the ZCode shared store (`adoptZcodeStore`)** — zero-loss convergence first (`lib/converge.js`: full backup of the local root → local-only files merged into the shared store → line-level union of MEMORY.md indexes → plain-file conflicts resolved by newer mtime, with the losing side preserved as a sibling `<name>.conflict-<side>-<timestamp>.md` copy), then the root switches; ZCode/CodeBuddy/DSH share one live store from then on — no sync jobs, no manual copying.
- **HGFS write fallback (`lib/write-fallback.js`)** — root cause pinned: the staged-fd `chmod` of dsh's local file backend always fails with `ENOENT fchmod` on HGFS (vmhgfs shares — the real home of the ZCode memory store), regardless of permissions; Writes/Edits inside the memory root that hit the defect automatically retry through native node:fs with identical semantics (temp-file publish, CRLF preserved, same version template); target comparison now uses "longest existing ancestor realpath + missing suffix", so 8.3 short paths and other spelling differences cannot bypass the fallback.
- Adoption is refused when `memoryRoot` is pinned by cordis.patch.yml (`adopt/patch-pinned`), ins

- **Fixed the import early-exit guard missing `copyProjects`** — when confirming an import into a brand-new target (no existing projects), whole-project copies were all skipped while the report still claimed success (`touched` only counted copyFiles+mergeIndexes); reproduced against a real 14-project / 244-file store, now lands everything, with the smoke test extended accordingly.

- **Verified against dsh 0.2.1-rc.5** — after the desktop app upgraded 0.2.1-rc.3 → 0.2.1-rc.5, the plugin keeps working unchanged (profile registration, memory injection, and the settings page all intact); no reinstall is needed across dsh patch-version upgrades. `engines.dsh` unchanged (the range already covers rc.5).

- **Settings page rework** — top-right search box on the file list (file name AND content search with match counts and context snippets); height-capped scrolling project/file lists; content preview below the list on click; **Browse…** (native directory chooser via the host's `remote.directoryPicker`) and **Open folder** (file-manager reveal via the official `session/openWorkspacePath`) buttons on the memory-root row.
- **Import from ZCode** — scan `~/.zcode/cli/memories` → show the diff plan (whole-project copies / new-file copies / line-merged indexes / name conflicts) → confirm → execute. Index merging is a deterministic line union (existing lines preserved, new lines appended, exact dedupe — minimal change, no model call); conflicting same-name files are kept and listed; ZCode-only references (`.zcode` paths, `zcode` CLI calls) are reported with fix suggestions for the user to decide; merged indexes are backed up to `<dsh-home>/dsh-zcode-memory/import-backup/<timestamp>/`.
- **Default memory root auto-created** — `<dsh-home>/memories/projects` is ensured at plugin startup and after saving a new root from the settings page.
- **Fault tolerance end to end** — gateway calls never r

- **Fix model-call failure on dsh 0.2.x** — `format v4 message requires a producer-owned source kind`: the v4 session format retired the generic `source: { kind: "plugin" }` wrapper, so injected memory context now carries the producer-owned kind `dsh-zcode-memory/memory-context`. Session log export no longer fails with HTTP 500 on sessions created by this version. (Sessions whose logs were written by v0.2.0 contain the retired kind and still fail export/replay on 0.2.x — delete those sessions.)

- **Support dsh 0.2.1-rc.3** — compatibility moved to `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0`; the typert contract was rewritten for the new `createTypertRemoteInfo` + lazy `create()` zod-factory format (the old `schema` field fails at boot on 0.2.x).
- **Installer version gate** — the installer reads the installed dsh version and refuses to install when it does not satisfy `engines.dsh` (dependency-free semver range evaluation); dsh CLI's own plugin gate acts as a second layer.
- **Changed-files panel handed to the official UI** — dsh 0.2.x ships `dsh-workspace-changes` + the new deliverables surface (turn tail with per-file diff and open actions) natively, so this plugin no longer carries its own 0.1-era client accumulator.
- **Desktop profile install documented** — the `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron app; see the install section for the manual manifest + pnpm steps.
- Verified against dsh 0.2.1-rc.3: plugin v0.2.0 active, the ZCode Memory settings section renders, and the remote gateway round-trips (11 ZCode-migrated projects listed).
- Initial release for dsh 0.1.0-rc.6: ZCode-compatible project memory, client-side post-turn changed-files panel with review/open, memory settings page.
